title: bug: a deploy to a REMOTE (ssh) target cannot deliver environment variables and now refuses
description:
Filed from task-0ca117e389df43ee9b458255f0752842 (the row that made a LOCAL deploy deliver its environment at all). Disclosed rather than hidden: that row's fix does not reach remote targets, and it now says so out loud instead of failing obscurely.

MEASURED, docker 29.6.2: a value passed with `--env` is printed by `docker inspect` in `.Config.Env` (1 grep hit); the same value in a BIND-MOUNTED FILE gives 0. `tests/e2e/foundation/platform-secret-canary.e2e.test.ts:218` sweeps that stdout and :232 asserts zero hits, so the delivery had to be a mounted file. A bind mount names a path on the DOCKER host, and for `sshTarget !== null` the docker host is not the daemon's — the path does not exist there.

WHAT IT DOES TODAY: `resolveCandidateMount` (apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-environment.ts) returns `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED` when `sshTarget !== null` AND the environment holds at least one variable; the deploy refuses before starting anything. A remote target whose environment holds NO variables still deploys exactly as before, so this is not a blanket removal of remote deploy.

WHY REFUSING BEATS MOUNTING ANYWAY: docker AUTO-CREATES a missing bind source as an empty DIRECTORY. The candidate would start, its loader would fail to read `/run/moe/env`, and the deploy would present as a 150-second DEPLOY_HEALTH_TIMEOUT with no hint of the cause.

THE SHAPE THAT WOULD FIX IT, already built and measured on this host before being set aside: `docker create` + `docker cp -` (a USTAR archive on stdin) + `docker start`. It needs no host file at all — the plaintext goes host memory -> docker CLI stdin -> container filesystem — and it works identically local and remote, because `run()` already carries stdin through `ssh <target> docker ...`. It was NOT taken on the parent row because it changes the candidate's docker VERB from `run` to `create`/`start`, and the verb is pinned well beyond the parent's planned blast radius: deploy-journey.test.ts:660, deploy-refusal-redaction.test.ts:325 (`failVerb("run")`), deploy-build-authority.test.ts:31, deploy-rollback.test.ts:183, deploy-service.test.ts:552/:779/:812/:850, and the double's dispatch at deploy-ports.ts:341. That is a rail-20 stop-and-report set, which is exactly why it is a row of its own.

Two facts any implementer needs, both measured: the image already carries `ENTRYPOINT ["docker-entrypoint.sh"]` from the node base image, and `--entrypoint` CLEARS `.Config.Cmd` — so the original `Entrypoint ++ Cmd` must be read back off the image (`imageCommandArgv`/`parseImageCommand` already do this).
definitionOfDone: A deploy to a target with sshTarget !== null delivers the environment store's variables to the candidate it starts, proven BY RESPONSE from the deployed build rather than by argv inspection.
No variable value reaches docker inspect, a log line, a receipt or an error path on the remote path either: the secret canary's candidate-inspect sweep still reports hits=0.
DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED is removed only once remote delivery actually works; until then it stays and is asserted by code, not merely by outcome.

Every consumer of the candidate's docker VERB is updated in the same commit (the nine sites enumerated in the description), with no exact toEqual loosened into a toContain and the positional arm at deploy-rollback.test.ts:142 left positional.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test EXIT 0 with its count line quoted, and the two MOE_PLATFORM_PIPELINE=1 e2e files stay green, run one at a time with --no-file-parallelism.

implementationPlan.description: Wire the candidate to create + copy + start, in deploy-service.ts. `startCandidate` at :226-232 is the ONLY caller of `runCandidateArgv` and the only seam that needs to change; `run(target, args, stdin?)` at :190-192 already threads stdin through both the local and the `ssh <target> docker ...` path, so no port and no capability is added. New sequence, replacing the single `run` call: `create` the candidate on the argv the leaf landed, then — only when the delivery holds variables — `docker cp -` the USTAR archive on STDIN into the container, then `start` it. THE VERB CHANGES UNCONDITIONALLY: do NOT keep a `run` path for the zero-variable case. Two start paths in a deploy engine is a maintenance hazard — a fix landed in one silently misses the other, and every future arm has to ask which it exercised — and DoD 4 enumerates the consumer sites on the assumption of one path. Preserve the existing replay semantics exactly: the `healthArgv(name)` probe still runs FIRST and an existing container is still reused rather than recreated, so a replay stays a replay and not a race. FAIL CLOSED ON EVERY LEG: a nonzero `create`, a nonzero `cp` or a nonzero `start` must refuse with the same code and layer discipline the current single-call failure uses, and a `cp` that fails must NOT leave a created-but-never-started container behind — epic rail 4 makes anything this row starts its job to stop, on the failure paths too. The plaintext goes host memory to docker CLI stdin to container filesystem and MUST NOT appear in any argv, so the value never becomes a token in the `cp` call.
implementationPlan.note:
WIRED, and the verb changed UNCONDITIONALLY — there is no `run` path left for the zero-variable case. `bringUpCandidate` probes `healthArgv(name)` FIRST (replay preserved byte for byte), then `create`, then `cp -` only when a delivery exists, then `start`.

THE SIZE CAP FORCED A NINTH PATH, and this is the only departure from the plan's eight. deploy-service.ts was 377 lines before this row; the inline seam took it to 419, past the hard 400 split bound. I extracted the seam into a NEW production module `apps/daemon/src/deployment/deploy-candidate-start.ts` (92 lines) holding `healthArgv`, `CandidateDelivery`, `prepareCandidateDelivery` and `bringUpCandidate`. deploy-service.ts is now 341 lines, deploy-candidate-environment.ts 232, the new file 92 — all three under 250. `healthArgv` MOVED there and is RE-EXPORTED from deploy-service.ts, so deploy-rollback.test.ts:9 and deploy-service.test.ts:31 keep importing it from the same place and neither needs an edit for the move; the new module is imported by nothing else, so it collides with no peer row.

THE SEAM, exactly as it now reads:
  const existing = await run(healthArgv(name)); if (existing.code === 0) return existing;
  const created = await run(createCandidateArgv(name, network, tag, delivery?.command ?? null));
  if (created.code !== 0) return created;
  if (delivery !== null) { const copied = await run(copyEnvironmentArgv(name), delivery.archive); if (copied.code !== 0) return copied; }
  return run(startCandidateArgv(name));
Every leg returns docker's own result VERBATIM, so `execute` refuses on the code and stderr docker produced — same code (DEPLOY_BUILD_FAILED) and same layer discipline the single-call failure used. No refusal is minted in the new module.

NO ORPHAN AFTER A FAILED cp OR start, through ONE teardown path rather than two that could disagree. `candidateStarted = true` is set BEFORE `startCandidate`, and `execute`'s existing `finally` already does `run(target, ["rm","--force",name])` under `candidateStarted && !keepCandidate && lease.incumbent !== name`. Since `startCandidate` now creates before it starts, that same line removes a created-but-never-started container. I added an explicit comment there saying so rather than adding a second rm inside the seam. Step 6 asserts it.

NO VALUE IN ANY ARGV. `copyEnvironmentArgv(name)` is `["cp","-","<name>:/"]`; the plaintext is the STDIN argument of `run(args, stdin)` and never a token. Confirmed against the leaf's builders, which carry no `--env`, no `--env-file` and no `--mount`.

TWO SHAPE CHANGES ANNOUNCED IN STEP 1, both landed, both confined to owned paths:
(a) `candidateEnvironmentPort` now returns `{ content: string | null, ok: true }` and WRITES NO FILE. `source`, `dispose`, the `mkdtempSync`/`writeFileSync`/`rmSync` machinery, `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_FILE_UNWRITABLE` and deploy-service's `disposeDelivery` + `finally` disposal are all gone. `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_FILE_UNWRITABLE` had zero consumers outside the module (git grep) and is unreachable by construction once nothing is written. The plaintext now exists only in process memory until the docker CLI reads it off stdin — no plaintext at rest on the daemon host at all, which is a strict improvement on epic rail 3 over the 0600 temp file.
(b) `resolveCandidateMount(run, sshTarget, tag, source)` became `resolveCandidateCommand(run, tag)` returning `readonly string[] | string`. It resolves the image's `Entrypoint ++ Cmd`, never a mount.

Production calls neither. tests/e2e/control-room/fake-docker-health-seed.test.ts:50/65 is not an owned path and pins the old verb through `runCandidateArgv`, and deploy-candidate-environment.test.ts:114 freezes its bytes as the migration baseline. Their doc comments now say "superseded, do not call from production" instead of claiming to be the live path.

implementationPlan.description: Remove the remote refusal — DoD 3, and only now that step 2 has made remote delivery reachable. In deploy-candidate-environment.ts: delete `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED` (:143) and the `if (sshTarget !== null) return ...` gate at the head of `resolveCandidateMount` (:128). The `sshTarget` parameter itself may become unused — remove it from the signature and from `candidateMount` at deploy-service.ts:235-237 rather than leaving a dead argument that reads as a live condition. REWRITE the doc comment at :135-142: it explains why a bind mount cannot reach a remote docker host and states "there is no `tee` to write with", which this row makes false; leaving it is a false record, and it is the sentence a future reader would trust. Replace it with what is now true — the archive travels on stdin, so nothing names a path on the docker host and local and remote are the same code path. DoD 3 requires the removal be asserted BY CODE, not merely by outcome: add an arm that reads the module source and asserts the constant name is absent, alongside a behavioural arm that a remote target with variables now resolves a delivery instead of a refusal string. Also update the module header (:10-46), which describes the mount-and-source-a-host-file design that this row replaces. Keep the file under 250 physical lines; the archive encoder lives in the leaf's `deploy-candidate-archive.ts`, not here.
implementationPlan.note:
DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED IS GONE, and only after step 2 made remote delivery reachable. The constant, the `if (sshTarget !== null) return ...` gate, the `sshTarget` and `source` parameters, and the "there is no `tee` to write with" doc block were all deleted together; `resolveCandidateMount` is now `resolveCandidateCommand(run, tag) => readonly string[] | string`. deploy-service.ts's `candidateMount` wrapper went with it.

ASSERTED BY CODE, NOT BY OUTCOME — the new arm "CANNOT refuse for being remote: there is no target-shaped parameter left to refuse on". It reads the SOURCE of all three production modules (deploy-candidate-environment.ts, deploy-candidate-start.ts, deploy-service.ts) and asserts the literal `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED` and the substring `REMOTE_UNSUPPORTED` are absent from every one. THREE THINGS STOP IT BEING VACUOUS: (a) each read asserts `source.length > 500`, so a renamed or missing module reds instead of reading as an empty string that trivially "does not contain" anything; (b) a POSITIVE CONTROL asserts `DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT_IMAGE_COMMAND_UNKNOWN` IS still present in the same bytes, so the sweep is proven able to find a literal; (c) `expect(resolveCandidateCommand.length).toBe(2)` pins the arity, so re-adding an `sshTarget` parameter reds even if the constant were spelled differently. Behavioural cover for the same clause is step 6's, against the docker double on a real `sshTarget !== null` target.

PROSE — the module header (:10-46) and the mount doc block were rewritten in step 2 rather than here, to avoid writing the same comments twice; this step verified they are true of the delivered code. They now say the delivery rides the docker CLI's stdin, that nothing names a path on the docker host, and that local and remote are the same code path. The test file's own header was updated for the same reason: it claimed "the only file written is the delivery file the port under test creates", which is now false.

THE PORT'S ARMS, rewritten around the shape change: "hands back the delivery TEXT and writes no file anywhere" replaces "writes an owner-only file outside the workspace, and disposes of it". It censuses `moe-deploy-env-*` in the OS temp directory before and after, asserts the set is UNCHANGED, and then plants a WITNESS directory with `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-deploy-env-"))` and asserts the census now DIFFERS — because "no new entries appeared" passes just as well against a filter that could never match, and this row's whole business is delivery paths that silently deliver nothing. The witness is removed in a `finally`. It also pins `Object.keys(delivered).sort()` to exactly `["content","ok"]`, so re-introducing a `source` or a `dispose` reds.

FILE SIZES, all under the caps: deploy-candidate-environment.ts 232 (was 250), deploy-candidate-start.ts 93, deploy-service.ts 366 (was 377 before this row — reduced, not grown; it was already over the 250 target and is well under the 400 bound).

NOTE FOR ANYONE RE-RUNNING THIS: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test -- <file>` does NOT narrow the run — the daemon's test script already ends in `src`, so the extra argument appends and the whole 606-file suite executes. Use the per-file recipe above.

implementationPlan.description: Migrate the five test sites that pin the verb NEGATIVELY — THE DANGEROUS HALF. Every one of these asserts that NO candidate was started, and after a verb rename each stays green while asserting nothing at all: deploy-build-authority.test.ts:31 (`some(args => args[0] === "run")).toBe(false)`), deploy-rollback.test.ts:183 (same shape), deploy-service.test.ts:552 (same shape), :812 and :850 (`filter(call => call[0] === "run")).toEqual([])`). Repoint each at the NEW verbs so it still fails when a candidate is started — assert no `create` AND no `start` for the candidate name, not merely no `run`. Then PROVE each one is non-vacuous individually: with the arm repointed, make the production path start a candidate on that scenario and confirm the arm goes RED. An arm asserting an absence that can no longer occur is worse than no arm, and these five are the exact sites where this migration would quietly hollow out the suite. implementationPlan.description: LIVE ACCEPTANCE — DoD 1 and DoD 2, and neither may be discharged by argv inspection or a fake runner. The owner agreed to bring Docker and the Windows OpenSSH server up for exactly this, and the target is `sshTarget = localhost`: that is a genuine `ssh <target> docker ...` path with real stdin carriage and a real container, so it satisfies DoD 1 literally without provisioning a remote host. DoD 1: deploy to a target with `sshTarget !== null`, holding at least one variable, and prove the variable arrived BY RESPONSE from the deployed build — the candidate answers an HTTP request echoing the value it read from its environment. Include the NEGATIVE CONTROL the parent row used: the incumbent answers with the marker absent BEFORE the flip, the candidate answers with it after, so the arm cannot pass against a build that never received anything. DoD 2: run the secret canary's candidate-inspect sweep on this remote path and record `swept=N artifacts, hits=0` with N quoted — a sweep that silently swept zero artifacts passes while proving nothing, so the denominator is load-bearing. Also sweep the `cp` call's own recorded argv and the deploy receipt. TEARDOWN IS PART OF THE ARM, not cleanup around it: every container, image, network and volume this acceptance creates is removed on EVERY exit path including the failure ones, and the run ends with a `docker ps -a` census proving nothing of yours survived. Epic rail 4 makes a leaked container or port inadmissible for every later gate on this board.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: THE ROW WAS SPLIT, and that is the main planning decision. The description names nine verb-pinning sites; the census I ran at HEAD found TWELVE, and after excluding three that watch the verifier's Postgres containers rather than the candidate (migrate-down-real.test.ts:100, rollback-restore-real.test.ts:123, tests/e2e/foundation/e2e-harness) the honest count for a single row was TEN distinct files, at the hard-reject boundary, one of them peer-dirty. So the argv builders, the USTAR encoder, the docker double's create/cp/start support and the control-room fake now live in leaf task-60f851fa3e1046fe98090d9dc6f30e0a (6 files, wires nothing, every existing `run` arm stays green WITHOUT edits), and this row owns the wiring, the refusal removal and the consumer migration (8 files). dependsOn is set to both the leaf and the already-DONE local-delivery producer. A VOLUME-BASED ALTERNATIVE was evaluated and rejected: `docker volume create` plus a populating `docker run --rm -i` writing the file into the volume from stdin would keep the candidate's verb as `run` and collapse the blast radius to about five files. It fails on its own terms — the populating call is itself a `run`, so the `filter(call => call[0] === "run")).toEqual([...])` arms move anyway whenever variables are present; it adds a volume to the teardown surface on a remote host, which epic rail 4 makes expensive; it needs `cat` in the candidate image, which is unmeasured; and it puts the plaintext through two containers instead of one. The create/cp/start shape was already built and measured on this host by the parent row's author before being set aside, and it is the one the row was filed to carry. KEEPING `run` FOR THE ZERO-VARIABLE CASE was also considered and rejected: it would preserve four negative arms untouched, but two start paths in a deploy engine means a fix landed in one silently misses the other and every future arm has to ask which it exercised. DoD 4 enumerates the consumer sites on the assumption of one path.
